# Manual Detection Pilot Checklist

Status: Validated
Specification Version: v1
Frozen: true
Type: General
Current Pass: 2

## Commandment Scores

| Pass | Commandment | State | Score | Why | Why not 100% | Escalated | Resolution |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Scope | Stable | 92% | User defined the checklist as the sole deliverable, explicitly stating no systems change. | Minor open ambiguity on exact document format/location, deferred to executor. | No | — |
| 1 | Constraints | Stable | 95% | D1 (approved): use the manual Friday review process for this pilot; owner explicitly declined automation. | Small residual ambiguity on pilot end-date/duration, not raised as material. | No | — |
| 1 | Risk | Stable | 90% | Owner explicitly accepted up to seven days of detection delay as a bounded, known risk for the pilot. | Owner being the sole reviewer at the two-Friday checkpoint (single point of failure) had not yet been surfaced. | No | — |
| 1 | Stakeholders | Stable | 95% | Owner self-assigned to inspect missed alerts after two Fridays; reporting team already runs the Friday review being reused as-is. | — | No | — |
| 1 | Harmony | Stable | 90% | Manual-only process, accepted delay, ownership, and review cadence are mutually consistent with a no-automation pilot. | — | No | — |
| 2 | Success | Stable | 95% | User explicitly defined "done" as: all four items present in the checklist, and no automation introduced — a crisp, testable criterion. | Slight risk that "presence" of an item could be satisfied by vague wording rather than usable content (see Misclassification Risks). | No | — |
| 2 | Verification | Stable | 90% | User confirmed the tradeoff is settled; verification is a manual read-through against the four required items, with the owner's post-two-Friday inspection serving as the operational feedback loop. | No automated/fast in-flight signal exists by design — this is an accepted tradeoff (D1), not a gap. | No | — |
| 2 | Execution Readiness | Stable | 92% | All four required content items, the no-automation constraint, and the success criteria are explicit and owner-confirmed this pass. | Document format/location is left to executor discretion (non-blocking). | No | — |
| 2 | Harmony | Stable | 92% | Re-checked after this pass's closure statement: four required items, no-automation constraint, and success criteria remain mutually consistent. | — | No | — |

## Problem Statement

The reporting team needs a single checklist artifact documenting an already-decided, manual-only detection pilot: reuse of the existing Friday review as the detection mechanism, an owner-accepted maximum seven-day detection delay, the owner's self-assignment to inspect missed alerts, and a review checkpoint after two Fridays. No automation or systems change is in scope — the checklist itself is the entire deliverable.

## Requirements

### R1
The checklist must document the existing manual Friday review as the detection mechanism for this pilot.

### R2
The checklist must document the accepted maximum seven-day detection delay.

### R3
The checklist must document the owner's self-assignment to inspect missed alerts.

### R4
The checklist must document the review checkpoint occurring after two Fridays.

### R5
The checklist must not introduce, propose, or reference any automation for detection or alerting (per D1).

## Constraints

### C1 (D1 — approved)
For this pilot, use the existing manual Friday review process. The owner has explicitly declined automation for the pilot.

### C2
No systems changes: the checklist is a documentation artifact only, not a code or infrastructure change.

### C3
Up to seven days of detection delay is an accepted, bounded limitation for the duration of the pilot.

## Success Criteria

### S1
The checklist document contains all four required items: Friday review, seven-day delay acceptance, owner assignment, and two-Friday review checkpoint (R1–R4).

### S2
The checklist introduces no automation components, tooling, or systems changes (R5).

## Validation Contract

### Acceptance Tests

- AT1: Manual read-through of the checklist confirms presence of all four required items (R1–R4), stated specifically enough to be actionable (not generic boilerplate).
- AT2: Manual read-through confirms no automation language or tooling is referenced anywhere in the checklist (R5).

### Regression Checks

None applicable — no existing system, code, or process is modified by this deliverable; the pilot reuses the existing Friday review unchanged.

### Failure Signals

- The checklist is missing any of the four required items.
- The checklist inadvertently proposes or references automated detection/alerting tooling.
- An item is present in name only (e.g., "delay accepted") without stating the specific commitment (e.g., "up to seven days").

### Verification Methods

Owner or reviewer manually inspects the checklist document against the four-item list (R1–R4) and the no-automation constraint (R5) before the pilot start.

### Feedback Loop Design

- In-progress signal: none needed before the checklist itself is delivered — it is a single static document. The relevant "in-flight" signal belongs to the pilot's operation, not the checklist's authoring: the owner's assigned inspection of missed alerts after two Fridays is the operational feedback loop.
- Cadence/cost: the owner reviews missed alerts once, roughly two weeks into the pilot, at the cost of her manual review time.
- Fallback if no fast signal exists: there is intentionally no automated/fast detection signal (accepted tradeoff, D1) — the two-Friday manual inspection is itself the fallback and the only checkpoint in this pilot.

### Known Blind Spots

- Any alert missed during the pilot may go undetected for up to seven days by design (accepted risk, D1).
- No mechanism catches misses between pilot start and the two-Friday inspection point other than the weekly Friday review itself.
- The owner is the sole reviewer at the two-Friday checkpoint; if she is unavailable, no alternate reviewer is defined (accepted, non-blocking — see Risks).

## Inputs

Existing manual Friday review process description; owner's decisions (D1) on delay tolerance, self-assignment, and review cadence.

## Outputs

A single checklist document listing the four required items (R1–R4).

## Out of Scope

- Automation of detection or alerting.
- Any systems or code changes.
- Changes to the review cadence or delay tolerance beyond this pilot.

## Authority Boundaries

### Executor May Decide

Checklist formatting, wording, and document location/filename.

### Executor Must Escalate

Any request to shorten the detection delay or introduce automation mid-pilot.

### Executor Must Not Change

The four required content items (R1–R4), or the D1 decision to use the manual-only process.

## Current Interpretation

The task is to produce a single checklist artifact for a reporting-team pilot that documents an already-decided manual process: the existing Friday review, an owner-accepted seven-day detection delay, the owner's self-assignment to inspect missed alerts, and a review checkpoint after two Fridays. No automation or system change is introduced; the checklist itself is the entire deliverable.

## Misclassification Risks

### Potential False Positives

A checklist that lists all four items in vague or boilerplate language could appear complete while not actually reflecting the owner's specific commitments — e.g., not stating "seven days" explicitly, not naming the owner's role, or not stating "after two Fridays" as the checkpoint timing — satisfying a shallow reading of R1–R4 without being usable in practice.

### Potential False Negatives

The checklist appears complete but omits an implicit expectation not explicitly requested, such as noting this is a pilot-scoped tradeoff (not a permanent policy), or what happens if the owner is unavailable on the two-Friday review date — details that would keep the checklist accurate as context shifts.

## Ambiguities

### Blocking

None remaining.

### Non-Blocking

Exact document format and storage location for the checklist (left to executor discretion per Authority Boundaries).

### Intentional

No escalation path is defined for missed alerts beyond the two-Friday inspection — accepted as out of scope for this pilot per D1.

## Risks

- Up to seven days of undetected alerts during the pilot (accepted, D1).
- Reliance on a single owner for manual inspection creates a single point of failure if she is unavailable at the two-Friday checkpoint (accepted, non-blocking; not escalated per Deferral Rule since it does not lower any commandment below 70%).

## Stakeholders

- Reporting team (users of the existing Friday review process).
- The owner (D1 decision-maker; self-assigned reviewer at the two-Friday checkpoint).
